question.problem:
$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{xy+2}{4}, & \,-1\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

The joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ for the continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is shown above. Given that 

$$
\text{E}[X]=\frac{1}{12},\,\text{E}[Y]=\frac{1}{2},\,\text{SD}[X]≈0.5713,\,\text{SD}[Y]≈0.2887,
$$

 
find the correlation coefficient of $X$ and $Y.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the correlation coefficient of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ is defined as

$$
\rho =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[Y]},
$$

where

- $\text{Cov}[X,Y]$ is the covariance, and

- $\text{SD}[X]$ and $\text{SD}[Y]$ are the standard deviations of $X$ and $Y.$

First, by applying the rule of the lazy statistician, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={∬}_{{R}^{2}}xy\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1}xy\cdot \frac{xy+2}{4}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{-1}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}{y}^{2}+2xy)\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{[\frac{{x}^{2}{y}^{3}}{3}+x{y}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=1}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{-1}^{1}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}+x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{[\frac{{x}^{3}}{9}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\frac{1}{9}+\frac{1}{2}-(-\frac{1}{9}+\frac{1}{2})] \\  & =\frac{1}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the covariance and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =\frac{1}{18}-(\frac{1}{12})(\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{72}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correlation coefficient is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\rho  & =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[Y]} \\  & ≈\frac{(\frac{1}{72})}{(0.5713)\cdot (0.2887)} \\  & ≈0.08,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
